issues.t: Transmission slips or gets stuck in second or third gear
issues.sym: Slipping, flaring revs between shifts, harsh or early shifts, or the truck suddenly staying in one gear (often second or third) with the check engine light on.
issues.why: The Ascender uses GM's 4L60-E four-speed automatic. GM issued bulletins for slipping (code P0757), cold-weather shift problems, and the transmission defaulting to a single gear, sometimes from an electrical short or a failing ignition switch rather than worn parts.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the fluid checked before agreeing to a rebuild; some cases are wiring or switch faults. If it slips badly or won't shift, drive gently and get it diagnosed soon.

issues.t: Cooling fan roars or engine runs hot from a failed fan clutch
issues.sym: A loud jet-like roar from the engine fan that won't stop, or the opposite: the temperature climbing in traffic. The check engine light may show fan clutch codes.
issues.why: The 4.2L six uses an electronically controlled fan clutch that commonly fails, either locking on or not engaging. GM issued a bulletin on fan clutch noise and diagnosis.
issues.next: If the temperature gauge climbs, pull over and let it cool; overheating can crack the head. Have the fan clutch and its wiring tested and replaced if faulty.

issues.t: Gas smell or fuel dripping from the tank area
issues.sym: A raw gasoline smell around the truck, wet spots or dripping under the fuel tank, or a fuel smell inside after filling up.
issues.why: Fuel lines at the top of the fuel pump module can corrode in salt-belt states and leak. NHTSA investigated, and GM extended the warranty on this part to 10 years or 120,000 miles; that coverage has likely ended.
issues.next: Don't drive or park it in a garage if you smell fuel or see drips; fuel leaks can catch fire. Have it towed to a shop to inspect the fuel pump module and lines.

issues.t: Fuel gauge reads wrong or drops to empty
issues.sym: The fuel gauge reads full or empty no matter how much is in the tank, jumps around, or the low-fuel light comes on early.
issues.why: The fuel level sensor inside the tank wears out. It is part of the fuel pump module, so the repair means dropping the tank.
issues.next: Track your mileage between fill-ups so you don't run out. Ask a shop to test the sending unit and give you a written quote before any repair.

issues.t: Check engine light from a cracked fuel filler neck
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with an evaporative (EVAP) leak code, and you may smell fuel near the filler door.
issues.why: The fuel filler neck can crack. GM extended coverage on it to 10 years or 150,000 miles, which has likely ended.
issues.next: Have the filler neck inspected if you see an EVAP code or smell fuel. A cracked neck can leak liquid fuel when the tank is full.

issues.t: Hard cold starts or rough running from clogged injectors
issues.sym: Long cranking on cold mornings, rough idle, hesitation, or a check engine light.
issues.why: Deposits can clog the fuel injectors. GM issued bulletins for driveability problems caused by clogged injectors.
issues.next: Ask a shop to test injector flow before replacing other parts. Cleaning or replacing the injectors usually fixes it.

issues.t: Long cranking from a cracked fuel sending unit port
issues.sym: The engine cranks a long time before starting, accelerates sluggishly, and the check engine light comes on.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin on a fracture in a port on the in-tank fuel sending unit that lets fuel pressure bleed off.
issues.next: Have a fuel pressure test done. The part sits in the tank, so the fix means lowering the tank.

issues.t: Engine misfires in wet weather
issues.sym: The engine stumbles, shakes or flashes the check engine light when driving in rain or after a car wash.
issues.why: Water can reach the spark plug area and cause misfires. GM's fix is to install a spark plug deflector.
issues.next: Have a shop read the misfire codes and check for the deflector and any damaged coil boots.

issues.t: Instrument panel gauges quit or act up
issues.sym: Gauges drop to zero, stick, or the whole cluster goes dark while driving. The speedometer may shake above 60 mph.
issues.why: Electrical faults in the instrument cluster and its connections were common on these years. GM also issued bulletins for an erratic or shaking speedometer.
issues.next: Watch your speed carefully until it is fixed. A shop can test the cluster; many are repaired rather than replaced.

issues.t: Ignition switch drains the battery or truck won't crank
issues.sym: A dead battery after the truck sits, or nothing happens when you turn the key.
issues.why: Faulty ignition switches can keep circuits powered and drain the battery. GM also issued a bulletin for intermittent no-crank, no-start conditions.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested first, then a parasitic draw test. Replace the ignition switch if it is the cause.

issues.t: ABS light on
issues.sym: The ABS warning light stays on, sometimes with the brake, traction or 4WD lights too.
issues.why: On 2005-06 trucks a wire near the A/C compressor pulley can chafe and set ABS faults. GM issued other bulletins for ABS lights tied to wheel speed sensor codes and lost communication with the brake module.
issues.next: Normal brakes should still work, but anti-lock won't. Have the codes read and the wiring checked before replacing the brake module.

issues.t: Airbag light stays on
issues.sym: The airbag (SRS) warning light stays on, or the passenger airbag status shows off when someone is seated.
issues.why: A faulty seat belt tension sensor can keep the light on. GM also issued bulletins for airbag codes on these years.
issues.next: Airbags may not work properly while the light is on. Have the SRS codes read and repaired soon.

issues.t: Blower runs on one speed, quits, or stays on
issues.sym: The fan won't blow on some settings, stops working, or keeps running with the key off.
issues.why: The blower motor control module on GM's midsize SUVs of this era (shared with the TrailBlazer and Envoy) commonly fails.
issues.next: Replace the blower control module. If the fan stays on with the truck off, unplug it until fixed to save the battery.

issues.t: Power window pops when going up
issues.sym: A popping noise as a window rises.
issues.why: The plastic guide on the window regulator, shared with the TrailBlazer, rubs against the glass.
issues.next: GM's fix is a strip of tape on the regulator where it touches the glass; the regulator usually doesn't need replacing.

issues.t: Steering groans when parking
issues.sym: A groan or shudder through the steering wheel during slow, tight turns.
issues.why: GM released redesigned steering gears for this platform, with a separate part for long-wheelbase models like the seven-passenger Ascender.
issues.next: Check the power steering fluid level first. If the groan persists, a shop can confirm whether the steering gear needs replacing.

issues.t: Liftgate glass hard to close or won't lock
issues.sym: The flip-up rear glass won't latch without slamming, or it won't lock and unlock with the key fob.
issues.why: The weather strip around the glass stiffens with age. GM also issued a bulletin for the liftgate glass lock not responding to the fob.
issues.next: A softer replacement weather strip and shim kit fixes the closing problem. Have the latch and wiring checked for the lock issue.

issues.t: Front clunk from worn stabilizer links
issues.sym: A rattle or clunk from the front over bumps or rough roads.
issues.why: The front stabilizer (sway) bar links wear out early on these years.
issues.next: Have the front end checked. Stabilizer links are inexpensive, but rule out ball joints and tie rods too.

issues.t: Water leaks at the windshield pillars
issues.sym: Wet carpet or headliner stains near the front corners of the cabin after rain.
issues.why: Water can get in at the A-pillars (the posts beside the windshield).
issues.next: Have a body shop water-test and reseal the area. Dry out wet carpet to prevent mold and electrical problems.

issues.t: Squeal or whistle from the front differential
issues.sym: A squeak, squeal or whistle from the front of the truck while driving.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for noise from the front differential on these SUVs.
issues.next: Have the front differential fluid and seals checked. Don't ignore growling that gets louder, which can mean bearing wear.

issues.t: Cracked exhaust manifold
issues.sym: A ticking or louder exhaust noise from the engine, especially when cold.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for exhaust manifolds cracking and causing increased exhaust noise.
issues.next: Have the manifold inspected. Exhaust leaks under the hood can let fumes into the cabin.

issues.t: StabiliTrak light stays on with code C0131
issues.sym: The StabiliTrak (stability control) warning light stays on.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for the stability control light with code C0131, which relates to the brake pressure sensor.
issues.next: Brakes still work, but stability control may not. Have the code read and the sensor diagnosed.

issues.t: Driver door switch can short and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Power windows or locks that work on and off, a burning smell or smoke from the driver door, even with the truck parked.
issues.why: Fluid can get into the driver door window switch module, corrode the circuit board and short it. GM recalled these trucks several times (12V406000, 13V248000, 14V404000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Until it is fixed, park outside and away from buildings. Stop using the switch if it acts up or smells hot.

issues.t: Headlights can go out (recall)
issues.sym: The low-beam headlights and daytime running lights stop working.
issues.why: The headlamp driver module can overheat and fail. GM recalled these trucks (15V519000) to replace it.
issues.next: If the headlights fail, don't drive at night. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Turn signals flash like hazards (recall)
issues.sym: Using the turn signal makes all the corner lights flash like hazards instead of one side.
issues.why: A faulty flasher module was replaced under recall 05V198000.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. Use hand signals if needed until it is fixed.

issues.t: Rear door latch can fail from corrosion (recall)
issues.sym: A rear door won't latch, won't open, or could open while driving.
issues.why: Road splash and salt can corrode the rear door latches. GM sealed the rocker area and cleaned or replaced latches under recall 05V494000.
issues.next: Keep rear doors locked and make sure they are fully closed. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Wipers stop or washer keeps running (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers won't turn on, stop mid-use, run on their own, or the washer keeps spraying.
issues.why: Water can get into the wiper module and short or corrode it. A recall (04V061000) repaired the wiper system.
issues.next: Don't drive in rain or snow without working wipers. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Key or shifter can leave Park without the brake (recall)
issues.sym: The key comes out with the shifter not in Park, or the shifter moves out of Park with the engine off.
issues.why: Mechanical overrides didn't meet federal theft-protection rules. A recall (03V213000) disabled them.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Power steering hose can burst (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden heavy steering, fluid leaking at the front, or smoke from under the hood.
issues.why: Some power steering hoses could crack during hard steering while braking, which can cause loss of assist and a fire if fluid hits hot parts. Recall 05V455000 replaced suspect hoses.
issues.next: If steering suddenly gets heavy or you see smoke, pull over and shut the engine off. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Windshield may not stay in place in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No sign in daily driving.
issues.why: The urethane bead holding the windshield may not bond fully to the body, so the glass may not stay in place in a crash. GM replaced affected windshields.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the windshield replaced if it is listed.

issues.t: Tire and load label lists the wrong capacity (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom. The sticker on the door jamb shows the wrong load capacity.
issues.why: The label overstated how much the truck can carry, which could lead to overloading or wrong tire pressure. Recall 05V552000 provided corrected labels.
issues.next: Don't load the truck to the label limit until you confirm you have the corrected label.
